transcript.answer: I could not find a rule in Lore saying code review must run on a different model family from the implementer, so I can't confirm one exists. What I found is only a practice. Lore's reviews (code-review, code-review-refine and code-review-recheck) were moved to gemini-3.1-pro-preview in September 2026. The recheck line had been on gemini-3.1-flash-lite. Only comment-triage stays on Haiku, and it is a routing call, not a review. Implementation agents appear to run on Claude, since the runner uses Claude Code. That makes the reviewer a different family in practice. The notes I found record the move to Gemini Pro as a model-tier change. They do not say it is required, and they do not say the reviewer must differ from the implementer. I did not find an ADR or spec stating such a constraint, but my searches were not exhaustive.

judgements.reason: The answer leans toward 'no rule', but it says that in practice the reviewer runs on a different family from a Claude implementer, whereas the gold answer says review was put on the implementation loop's own family; it also misses ADR-039 and the 2026-10-14 amendment.
